title: MOSFETs: gate drive, resistance and safe operation
summary: Read an N-channel power MOSFET as a voltage-driven switch whose gate still demands current while changing state.

blocks.title: The gate is insulated, but it is not free
blocks.body: A MOSFET gate draws little steady DC current in normal operation. Every transition still moves charge, and the driver, layout and switching speed decide how cleanly the device crosses its high-loss region.

columns.name: Gate-to-source voltage, VGS
columns.detail: Controls channel formation. It must be measured at the device source, not assumed from a controller’s nominal output.

columns.name: Drain-to-source voltage, VDS
columns.detail: Appears across the load path. It is limited by device rating and transient conditions.

columns.name: Gate threshold, VGS(th)
columns.detail: A test point near the beginning of conduction at a small specified drain current. It is not the gate voltage that guarantees low RDS(on).

blocks.heading: 2. Use the guaranteed on-resistance row
blocks.body: RDS(on) is specified at stated gate drive, drain current and junction temperature. Conduction loss is approximately I² × RDS(on) for the resistive interval, so current hurts twice and hot resistance is often higher than the headline room-temperature value. Use the appropriate maximum value and temperature information, then evaluate the complete thermal path.

blocks.heading: 3. Follow a switching edge
items: The driver sources current to charge the gate. Gate voltage rises toward the threshold while drain current begins to change.
During the Miller interval, drain voltage changes while gate voltage can pause. Driver current, gate charge and circuit conditions set the transition time.
Once fully enhanced, conduction loss dominates if switching is slow relative to on-time.
At turn-off the driver must remove gate charge. Parasitic inductance and capacitance can produce ringing or unintended gate movement, so layout and drive impedance matter.

blocks.title: Absolute maximum is a boundary, not a design target
blocks.body: Keep normal operation away from maximum VGS, VDS, current, power and junction-temperature limits. Check transient energy, avalanche conditions and safe operating area when the application can expose them.

blocks.heading: 4. Check the model
blocks.prompt: A MOSFET has VGS(th) between 1 V and 2.5 V, while RDS(on) is specified at 4.5 V and 10 V. Which value decides whether a 3.3 V driver guarantees the stated low resistance?
options: A guaranteed RDS(on) specification at 3.3 V, if the datasheet provides one.
blocks.explanation: Threshold only marks the beginning of conduction. Without a guaranteed on-resistance at the available gate drive, the low resistance is not guaranteed.

items.label: Copy the exact part number
items.detail: Package and suffix can change ratings and thermal behavior.

items.label: Mark the guaranteed gate drives
items.detail: List every VGS value used in the RDS(on) specifications and curves.

items.label: Estimate losses
items.detail: Record current, hot RDS(on), switching frequency, gate charge and the assumptions behind the estimate.

items.label: Check the boundaries
items.detail: Record VGS, VDS, junction temperature, safe-operating-area and transient limits that apply.
